name: Mohammed bin Salman
role: Crown Prince & Prime Minister, Saudi Arabia
quote: Signed both the 2025 Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement with Pakistan and the 2026 Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Turkey and Pakistan, positioning Saudi Arabia as the pact's financing hub and secretariat host.

name: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan
quote: Signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement on Aug 7, 2026, bringing Turkey's NATO-linked military and defense-industrial base into the trilateral pact.

name: Shehbaz Sharif
quote: Signed both the 2025 SMDA and the 2026 Mecca pact, embedding Pakistan — the pact's only nuclear-armed member — in Middle Eastern security architecture.

name: Ishaq Dar
quote: "The Makkah Accord does not abrogate or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between these countries, or with other countries or organizations."

name: Hakan Fidan
quote: "Under our president's vision, we should not remain limited to three countries. We should grow and, if necessary, bring [other] countries under this umbrella."

name: Abbas Araghchi
quote: Called on Muslim states to "rely only on ourselves and embrace true brotherhood" in response to the Mecca pact's announcement, without directly criticizing it.

name: Ebrahim Rezaei
role: Member, Majlis National Security Commission, Iran
quote: Dismissed the Mecca pact as a "paper agreement" that would bring Saudi Arabia no real security, urging Riyadh to "correct its policies so that it would no longer need to seek security from others."

name: Masoud Pezeshkian
quote: Welcomed the 2025 Saudi-Pakistan pact as the start of a "comprehensive regional security system" opposing Israeli military expansion — a warmer tone than Iran's later, more skeptical response to the trilateral Mecca pact.

name: Benjamin Netanyahu
quote: Office declined formal comment on the Mecca pact; reportedly floated the concept of a "Hexagon Alliance" as a counter-initiative and lobbied Washington against F-35 sales to Turkey.

name: Amichai Chikli
quote: Warned Israel should prepare for the possibility of military confrontation with Turkey, including at sea, in the wake of the Mecca pact.

name: Yoel Guzansky
role: Analyst, Institute for National Security Studies (Israel)
quote: "An alignment, perhaps. It has goals, but not necessarily military ones" — noting Turkey made 'no declaration of war against the Houthis' despite the pact when Saudi Arabia was recently attacked.

name: Abdulkhaleq Abdulla
quote: "One of the paradoxes of time" that a country a quarter of whose population is poor and a third illiterate could "opportunistically" position itself to defend Saudi Arabia — mocking Pakistan's role in the pact in a viral X post that drew backlash and exposed continued UAE unease over the agreement.

name: Steven A. Cook
quote: "After five decades, it is no longer possible to talk about a U.S.-led order in the Middle East" — arguing the Mecca pact proves regional powers are now shaping their own security order.

name: Blaise Misztal
role: Analyst, Jewish Institute for National Security of America
quote: Warned the three signatories' "only strategic rationale that unites them all is an incompatible one," since each seeks regional leadership without accepting the others' primacy.

role: Spokesperson, Ministry of External Affairs, India
name: MEA Spokesperson (India)
quote: Said India is "closely following" the Mecca pact's development and expects Riyadh to consider India's "interests and sensitivities."

name: Donald Trump
quote: "Very happy to see that Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan have recently, and finally, signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement" — said the pact "shows that the Middle East is coming together" (Truth Social, Aug 17, 2026).

name: Humayun Kabir
quote: "Bangladesh maintains a positive approach towards the possibility of joining an economic or defence framework involving Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye, taking into account its own interests and the changing dynamics of the global economy and trade."

name: Mehdi Rahimi
role: Head, Khaneh Mellat (Iranian Parliament News Agency)
quote: "Iran has received an invitation to join the Mecca Agreement, and the matter is under review" — calling it "a victory for Iran, because it has been calling for this for a long time" (Al Mayadeen, Aug 23, 2026).

name: Esmail Baghaei
quote: "We have not received a formal invitation, but proposals have been raised for dialogue with these countries on matters related to collective security in the region" — contradicting an Iranian parliamentary official's claim from the previous day (Aug 24, 2026).
